content.rationale: A release is the version substitution followed by `cargo publish`, and nothing else, so the gate is runnable rather than reviewed: tests/version_release/version_release_test.py runs the entry point that the decision puts under scripts/ in throwaway copies of the tree, with cargo, dist, gh, git, jj, curl and wget replaced by recording stubs, so no build, no network and no repository is touched. The copies differ only in what the version record (nodes/nlomlqum.json) and the manifest (trolstmt's Cargo.toml) carry, so the token is the only thing the substitution can follow. Each sandbox is a copy of the tree as it stands, planted with nothing and stripped of nothing, because the decision leaves the release no configuration file to read; the probe requires no release-layout file to exist and requires no CI to call the entry point, and it observes a release that cannot run without such a file as one that fails to substitute and publish. Success is observed once per documented interface form — the named version as a positional argument, as --version <v>, as --tag v<v>, as a bare v<v>, as VERSION=<v> in the environment, and on standard input, each form given its own distinct version — because the release node documents that a caller may name the version in any of those six forms and the gate holds the entry point to that documented interface: an entry point that accepts only one form leaves a caller who names the version another way unreleased, so every form has to substitute on its own and each form that does not is named. It conforms when: the record holds T and the manifest carries T, and the manifest's [package] version becomes the requested version; a substituted record T' (not T) with the manifest carrying T' still becomes the requested version, so a literal built into the entry point does not satisfy it; the same tree asked for a second, different named version puts that second version in the manifest, so the version that lands is the one the caller names; the tree whose manifest already carries the requested version is released rather than refused — exit 0, the manifest still carrying that version, and the publish still driven — because the decision allows the substitution to be a no-op there and that is the only state that can release the current tree, checked for each requested version so a no-op keyed to one literal value does not pass; a record holding T while the manifest carries a version the record does not carry and does not equal the request, and a missing record, each make the entry point exit non-zero, drive no step and leave the manifest as it was, rather than overwrite a version the record does not name; the conforming run exits 0, since a non-zero exit is a failed release; the run drives `cargo publish` and the stub records the manifest version at the moment of that invocation, so the recorded publish has to be preceded by the substitution — a publish issued while the manifest still carried the token is named — because publishing before the substitution publishes the token rather than the release; and with the `cargo publish` stub exiting non-zero the entry point exits non-zero and drives no later step, where stopping is observed as no publish invocation recorded after the failing one, rather than inferred. The removal is checked the same way: an invocation of dist, or of `gh release`, during a release is named as machinery the decision took out — the prebuilt binaries, the installers and the GitHub hosting — so a release that still builds, hosts or plans through dist does not conform. One accepted form is reused to offer the second version, so the version that lands is the one the caller names rather than a literal the entry point carries. It needs no cargo build, no dist install and no network, and tracks the recorded token rather than the decision's wording.
